workflows.name: PR Review
workflows.description: PR Review + Merge workflow for OpenFox

steps.name: Setup Workspace
steps.prompt:
Set up the review workspace for PR #{{pr_number}}:

1. Use the `workspace` tool to switch to a new workspace named `review-pr-{{pr_number}}`
2. Point origin to GitHub: `git remote set-url origin git@github.com:co-l/openfox.git`
3. Fetch and sync with develop: `git fetch origin && git reset --hard origin/develop`
4. Checkout the PR branch: `gh pr checkout {{pr_number}}`

If `gh pr checkout` fails because the PR head branch name collides with a local branch (e.g. the PR head is also named `develop`), fetch the PR head ref directly instead:
`git fetch origin refs/pull/{{pr_number}}/head && git checkout -b pr-{{pr_number}}-head FETCH_HEAD`

If any step fails, report the error and call step_done(). Otherwise call step_done().

steps.name: Verify Base Branch
steps.prompt:
Verify the PR #{{pr_number}} targets develop:

1. Check the base branch: `PR_BASE=$(gh pr view {{pr_number}} --json baseRefName --jq '.baseRefName')`
2. If it's not "develop", retarget it: `gh api repos/co-l/openfox/pulls/{{pr_number}} -X PATCH -f base=develop && git fetch origin`
3. Rebase onto latest develop: `git rebase origin/develop`

If rebase has conflicts, abort with `git rebase --abort` and report them. Otherwise call step_done().

steps.name: Review & Report
steps.prompt:
Review PR #{{pr_number}} and present findings:

1. Read the diff: `git diff origin/develop...HEAD`
2. List changed files: `git diff --stat origin/develop...HEAD`
3. Run: `npm run test && npm run typecheck && npm run lint`
4. Inspect code quality, error handling, edge cases

Present a clear summary to the user:
- What was reviewed
- Key findings with specific line references
- Whether any fixes are needed (be specific about what and why)
- If no fixes needed, state that clearly

Call step_done() when done.

steps.name: Apply Fixes
steps.prompt:
Apply the fixes you identified during review:

1. Implement the agreed fixes and improvements.
2. Verify with: `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run test`
3. Leave everything UNCOMMITTED. Do NOT commit, tag, or push anything — the single review commit happens after manual testing.

If there is nothing to fix or apply, say so explicitly and call step_done().

steps.name: Start Dev Server
steps.prompt:
Start the dev server using the `dev_server` tool so the user can manually test the changes. Once it's running, present a handoff summary:

> **PR #{{pr_number}} is ready at http://localhost:<port>.**
>
> **What I fixed:**
> - _bullet list of specific changes_
> - _why each matters_
> - _if no fixes were needed, say so explicitly instead of an empty list_
>
> **What to test:**
> - _specific things to try from the user's perspective_
> - _edge cases_

Do NOT ask the user if they want the dev server started — just start it and present the summary. Call step_done() when done.

steps.name: Commit All Fixes & Adjustments
steps.prompt:
All fixes and testing adjustments are now in the review workspace. Capture them in ONE commit:

1. `git add -A`
2. If there are staged changes: `git commit -m "review: fixes for PR #{{pr_number}}"`
   If nothing is staged, report that there is nothing to commit.
3. Tag the tip so it can be located later: `git tag -f review-fixes-{{pr_number}}`
4. Push the tag: `git push origin review-fixes-{{pr_number}}`
5. Report whether fixes were captured (yes/no) and call step_done().

steps.name: Prepare PR for Merge
steps.prompt:
Make sure PR #{{pr_number}} is mergeable before attempting the squash-merge:

1. Check mergeability and PR head details:
   `gh pr view {{pr_number}} --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus,headRepositoryOwner,headRefName,maintainerCanModify`
2. If `mergeable` is "MERGEABLE": report it and call step_done() — the squash-merge step can proceed.
3. If the PR is conflicting or otherwise not mergeable, rebuild the PR head on latest develop so it merges cleanly:
   a. `git fetch origin && git fetch origin refs/pull/{{pr_number}}/head`
   b. Create a fresh branch from the latest develop: `git checkout -b pr-{{pr_number}}-merged origin/develop`
   c. Bring in the PR content plus all local review fixes (the `review-fixes-{{pr_number}}` tag from the capture step): `git merge --squash review-fixes-{{pr_number}}`
   d. Resolve every conflict — when both sides add features, keep BOTH; never delete the other side's code.
   e. Verify: `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run test`, then `git add -A && git commit -m "PR #{{pr_number}}: merged onto develop"`.
   f. Push the resolved head to the PR's head ref (only possible when `maintainerCanModify` is true):
      `git push --force-with-lease=<headRefName>:<expectedSha> https://github.com/<headOwner>/<headRepo>.git pr-{{pr_number}}-merged:<headRefName>`
   g. Re-check mergeability with step 1.
4. If the PR still is not mergeable, or pushing to the fork's head is not possible, report the blocker explicitly so the user can intervene, then call step_done().

steps.name: Squash-Merge PR
steps.prompt:
Squash-merge PR #{{pr_number}} via API:

1. `gh api repos/co-l/openfox/pulls/{{pr_number}}/merge -X PUT -f merge_method=squash -f commit_title="PR #{{pr_number}}: $(gh pr view {{pr_number}} --json title --jq '.title')"`
2. Call step_done().

steps.name: Confirm Merge on Develop
steps.prompt:
Switch to original and confirm the merge landed on develop:

1. `workspace switch original`
2. `git checkout develop && git pull origin develop --ff-only`
3. Confirm the squash-merge commit exists: `git log --oneline -3 develop` (look for `PR #{{pr_number}}: ...`).
4. The review fixes were folded into that single squash commit (one-commit design), so no separate cherry-pick is needed. If the squash commit is missing, report it loudly.
5. Call step_done().

steps.name: Verify Fixes on Origin
steps.prompt:
Verify the PR's changes are present in git history on both local and origin develop, before deleting the workspace:

1. `git fetch origin` then confirm local and remote are in sync: `git rev-parse develop origin/develop` (SHAs must match)
2. Confirm the PR's squash-merge commit (`PR #{{pr_number}}: ...`) is in history on both: `git log --oneline -5 develop` and `git log --oneline -5 origin/develop`
3. If review fixes were applied: they are folded into the single squash-merge commit (one-commit design) — there is no separate `review: fixes for PR #{{pr_number}}` commit on develop. State that and confirm the fix content is present by spot-checking one of the fixed files: `git show origin/develop:<file>`
4. Spot-check the merged changes exist on origin: pick a file the PR touched and confirm via `git show origin/develop:<file>`

Report whether the changes are confirmed on both local and origin, then call step_done().

steps.name: Clean Up
steps.prompt:
Remove temporary artifacts and delete the workspace:

1. Remove remote tag if it exists: `git push origin --delete refs/tags/review-fixes-{{pr_number}} 2>/dev/null; true`
2. Remove local tag if it exists: `git tag -d review-fixes-{{pr_number}} 2>/dev/null; true`
3. `workspace delete review-pr-{{pr_number}}`
4. Call step_done().

steps.name: Leave Feedback on PR
steps.prompt:
Leave closing feedback on PR #{{pr_number}} once the user has approved it:

1. Determine the next release version: read the current version from package.json and use the next patch bump (e.g. 2.0.112 -> v2.0.113). If you can't determine it confidently, ask the user.
2. Draft the PR comment with EXACTLY this format (the `### AI-summary` heading is mandatory, no AI-written intro paragraph). The AI-summary bullets describe what WE, the maintainers, did on this PR during the review — rebase, conflict resolution, fixes applied, verification — NOT the PR's own feature content:

Merged, will be released in vX.Y.Z
---
### AI-summary
- <bullet point>
- <bullet point>

Example:

Merged, will be released in v2.0.132
---
### AI-summary
- Rebased the PR onto latest develop and resolved merge conflicts with the LLM capability tables (kept both branches' capabilities)
- Fixed the affected tests to match the merged types and verified the whole suite (unit + e2e green, typecheck and lint clean)
- Pushed the rebased branch to the contributor's fork so the PR merges cleanly with full attribution

3. Present the full draft in chat and ask the user to approve or modify it.
4. Do NOT post the comment until the user explicitly approves the final text.
5. Once approved, post it: write the text to a temp file and run `gh pr comment {{pr_number}} --body-file <tempfile>`, then remove the temp file.

Call step_done() when you have presented the draft.

skills.name: handoff
skills.description: Compact the current conversation into a handoff document for another agent to pick up.
skills.prompt:
Write a handoff document summarising the current conversation so a fresh agent can continue the work. Save to the temporary directory of the user's OS - not the current workspace.

Include a "suggested skills" section in the document, naming which skills the next agent should call the Skill tool for.

Do not duplicate content already captured in other artifacts (specs, plans, ADRs, issues, commits, diffs). Reference them by path or URL instead.

Redact any sensitive information, such as API keys, passwords, or personally identifiable information.

If the user passed arguments, treat them as a description of what the next session will focus on and tailor the doc accordingly.

skills.name: context7-mcp
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks about libraries, frameworks, API references, or needs code examples. Activates for setup questions, code generation involving libraries, or mentions of specific frameworks like React, Vue, Next.js, Prisma, Supabase, etc.
skills.prompt:
When the user asks about libraries, frameworks, or needs code examples, use Context7 to fetch current documentation instead of relying on training data.

## When to Use This Skill

Activate this skill when the user:

- Asks setup or configuration questions ("How do I configure Next.js middleware?")
- Requests code involving libraries ("Write a Prisma query for...")
- Needs API references ("What are the Supabase auth methods?")
- Mentions specific frameworks (React, Vue, Svelte, Express, Tailwind, etc.)

## How to Fetch Documentation

### Step 1: Resolve the Library ID

Call `resolve-library-id` with:

- `libraryName`: The library name extracted from the user's question
- `query`: The user's full question (improves relevance ranking)

### Step 2: Select the Best Match

From the resolution results, choose based on:

- Exact or closest name match to what the user asked for
- Higher benchmark scores indicate better documentation quality
- If the user mentioned a version (e.g., "React 19"), prefer version-specific IDs

### Step 3: Fetch the Documentation

Call `query-docs` with:

- `libraryId`: The selected Context7 library ID (e.g., `/vercel/next.js`)
- `query`: The user's specific question

### Step 4: Use the Documentation

Incorporate the fetched documentation into your response:

- Answer the user's question using current, accurate information
- Include relevant code examples from the docs
- Cite the library version when relevant

## Guidelines

- **Be specific**: Pass the user's full question as the query for better results
- **Version awareness**: When users mention versions ("Next.js 15", "React 19"), use version-specific library IDs if available from the resolution step
- **Prefer official sources**: When multiple matches exist, prefer official/primary packages over community forks

skills.name: browser-tester
skills.description: Interactive browser testing guidelines using @playwright/cli in headed mode (visible window) for live user inspection, supporting mobile viewport resizing (390x844), Groupama proxy auth dialogs, and local dev server targeting.
skills.prompt:
# Interactive Browser Testing via @playwright/cli (Headed Mode)

This skill guides interactive web and UI validation using `@playwright/cli` in **headed mode** (`--headed`), ensuring testing targets the **local development server** (`http://localhost:<port>`), supports **mobile app viewports** (`resize 390 844`), and handles network/proxy challenges.

---

## 1. Target URL Resolution (Local First)

- **Local Development Server (Default)**: Always target the local development URL (e.g. `http://localhost:11469`, `http://localhost:8080`, or `http://localhost:3000`) where recent code changes are running.
- **Remote Validation (`rec`/`pprod`)**: Only open remote environments when explicitly requested to test remote SSO/GConnect deployments.
- **NEVER Open Production**: Production URLs must never be targeted during development testing.

---

## 2. Mobile Viewport Sizing (`is_mobile_project`)

When testing mobile applications (Ionic, Capacitor, mobile web) or when `is_mobile_project` is `yes` / `true`:
- Immediately after opening the browser, resize the viewport to standard mobile dimensions:
  ```bash
  npx -y @playwright/cli resize 390 844
  ```
- This ensures mobile UI components (Ionic menus, tabs, toolbars, touch targets) render accurately in the visible window.

---

## 3. Core Principles & Human Assistance

- **Headed Mode (Always Visible)**: Always launch the browser with the `--headed` flag so the user can see the window, monitor progress, and take over or intervene if an unexpected modal, CAPTCHA, or blocked state occurs.
- **Handling Groupama Proxy / F5 Popups**:
  - If a proxy authentication dialog (`vip-f5-as-proxy...`) appears, pause and ask the user via `ask_user` to enter their corporate credentials in the open Chromium window.
  - Resume testing as soon as the user confirms.
- **Snapshot-first Interaction**: Run `snapshot` to identify element reference IDs (e.g. `e42`), then interact using those references.
- **Always Close When Done**: Prevent lingering processes and CPU leaks by calling `close` at the end of the test execution.

---

## 4. Test Execution Sequence

1. **Load Skills**:
   ```bash
   load_skill browser
   load_skill launch-dev-server
   load_skill connexion-gconnect
   ```

2. **Ensure Dev Server Is Running**:
   - Verify local dev server is active (via `dev_server` status or local port check).

3. **Open Target Application (Headed / Visible Window)**:
   ```bash
   npx -y @playwright/cli open --headed http://localhost:<port>
   ```
   > The browser window opens visibly on the user's desktop.

4. **Apply Mobile Viewport If Applicable**:
   ```bash
   # If mobile project (is_mobile_project: yes)
   npx -y @playwright/cli resize 390 844
   ```

5. **Interact and Drive Scenarios**:
   - Take snapshot to get element IDs:
     ```bash
     npx -y @playwright/cli snapshot
     ```
   - Click elements / buttons:
     ```bash
     npx -y @playwright/cli click <REF_ID>
     ```
   - Fill inputs and forms:
     ```bash
     npx -y @playwright/cli fill <REF_ID> "<VALUE>"
     ```
   - Press keys:
     ```bash
     npx -y @playwright/cli press Enter
     ```

6. **Handling Blocked States & User Intervention**:
   - If an element is missing, proxy credentials are required, or GConnect / 2FA needs manual attention:
     - Run `npx -y @playwright/cli snapshot` to capture the current state.
     - Prompt the user using `ask_user`.
     - The user can directly interact with the visible browser window.
     - Re-run `npx -y @playwright/cli snapshot` to detect the updated state after user action.

7. **Visual & DOM Verification**:
   - Verify state through snapshots:
     ```bash
     npx -y @playwright/cli snapshot
     ```
   - Capture screenshot if needed:
     ```bash
     npx -y @playwright/cli screenshot
     ```

8. **Clean Up & Shutdown**:
   ```bash
   npx -y @playwright/cli close
   ```

---

## 5. Reporting Failures

If a test fails or UI behavior violates acceptance criteria:
- Record the failure details, expected vs actual behavior, and reproduction steps in `session_metadata` (key: `test_findings`, status: `open`).
- Always run `npx -y @playwright/cli close` before concluding.

skills.name: build-install-mobile-app
skills.description: Guidelines and commands to build, package, and install native mobile applications on local simulators/emulators according to the selected environment (rec, pprod, local) and project-specific scripts.
skills.prompt:
# Mobile App Build & Simulator Installation Guide

This skill provides a deterministic, fast build and installation procedure for mobile applications (Ionic, Capacitor, Cordova, React Native, Native iOS/Android) targeting a specific environment (`rec`, `pprod`, or `local`).

---

## 1. Environment Determination

The target environment determines the build configuration, API endpoints, and configuration files:

1. **When running within a workflow**:
   - The target environment is provided directly in the prompt as `{{target_env}}` (`rec` or `pprod`, default `pprod`).
2. **When running standalone**:
   - Default to `pprod` or ask user if ambiguous.

---

## 2. Direct iOS Simulator Setup & Build Playbook (Ionic / Capacitor)

Follow this direct sequence without intermediate exploratory steps (do **NOT** search `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData`):

### Step 1: Discover / Boot Simulator
1. Query available booted devices:
   - Call `mobile-mcp_mobile_list_available_devices`.
2. If no device is online/booted:
   ```bash
   DEVICE_ID=$(xcrun simctl list devices available | grep -E "iPhone 1[5-7]|iPhone" | head -n 1 | grep -oE '[A-F0-9-]{36}')
   xcrun simctl boot "$DEVICE_ID" && open -a Simulator
   ```
3. Store `<DEVICE_ID>`.

### Step 2: Sync Web Assets
- If `package.json` contains `sync-ios-<env>`:
  ```bash
  npm run sync-ios-<env>
  ```
  *(e.g., `npm run sync-ios-pprod` or `npm run sync-ios-rec`)*
- Otherwise:
  ```bash
  npm run build && npx cap sync ios
  ```

### Step 3: Build directly to Local DerivedData
- Build scheme `<env>` (e.g. `pprod` or `rec` or `App`) targeting local `build/derivedData`:
  ```bash
  xcodebuild -workspace ios/App/App.xcworkspace \
    -scheme <env> \
    -configuration Debug \
    -destination "id=<DEVICE_ID>" \
    -derivedDataPath build/derivedData build
  ```
- The generated application bundle will always reside at:
  `build/derivedData/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/<env>.app`

### Step 4: Install App
```bash
xcrun simctl install "<DEVICE_ID>" "build/derivedData/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/<env>.app"
```

### Step 5: Read Bundle ID & Launch
1. Extract Bundle Identifier:
   ```bash
   BUNDLE_ID=$(defaults read "$(pwd)/build/derivedData/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/<env>.app/Info.plist" CFBundleIdentifier)
   ```
2. Launch into foreground:
   ```bash
   xcrun simctl launch "<DEVICE_ID>" "$BUNDLE_ID"
   sleep 3
   ```
3. Confirm active UI:
   - Call `mobile-mcp_mobile_list_elements_on_screen(device: "<DEVICE_ID>")`.

---

## 3. Direct Android Emulator Setup & Build Playbook

1. Check running emulators: `adb devices`.
2. Build debug APK:
   ```bash
   cd android && ./gradlew assembleDebug && cd ..
   ```
3. Install:
   ```bash
   adb -s "<DEVICE_ID>" install -r android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk
   ```
4. Launch via `adb shell monkey -p <PACKAGE_NAME> -c android.intent.category.LAUNCHER 1` and wait 3s.
